The Derivative of the Mixed Block in the Hyperparameters

Source: R/marginal_derivatives.R
penalty_dcross.Rd

Returns \(\partial^3\rho/\partial\beta\,\partial\theta_m\partial\theta_l\), one coefficient vector per unordered pair. penalty_cross() gives the derivative of the coefficient gradient in one hyperparameter, and this generic gives the derivative of that quantity in a second hyperparameter.

Usage

penalty_dcross(penalty, beta, theta, ...)

Arguments

penalty

A penalty() object.

beta

A numeric vector of length penalty@n_coef; the generic signals an error for any other length. The structured and separable branches read its values; the quadratic and additive branches return zero for any value.

theta

A named list of hyperparameter values, or a named numeric vector carrying the same, checked by the generic as in penalty_dhessian().

...

Passed to methods. The shipped methods do not read it.

Value

A named list of one numeric vector of length penalty@n_coef per unordered pair, keyed diagonals first.

Details

A marginal criterion is evaluated at the penalized mode, and the mode moves with the hyperparameters. The second derivative of the criterion therefore contains the second derivative of the mode, and this quantity is the contribution of the penalty to it.

It is exactly zero wherever the penalty is quadratic in the coefficients with a Hessian linear in the hyperparameters, which covers the quadratic and additive branches. The structured branch returns \((\partial^2\Omega/\partial\theta_m\partial\theta_l)\beta\), computed from penalty_d2hessian(), and the separable branch returns \(-D'(\partial^3\ell/\partial y\,\partial\theta_m\partial\theta_l)\), from distributions7::distrib_grad_y_hess() of the parent evaluated at \(D\beta\).

The keys are those of penalty_hess_theta(), diagonal pairs first.

See also

penalty_cross() for the first order, penalty_dhessian() and penalty_d2hessian() for the other two quantities that a marginal criterion requires.

Examples

b <- c(1, -0.5, 0.3)

# The derivative is zero on the quadratic branch.
penalty_dcross(quadratic_penalty(diag(3)), b, list(lambda = 2))
#> $lambda_lambda
#> [1] 0 0 0
#> 

# It is not zero on the structured branch, where it equals
# d2 Omega / dtheta^2 times the coefficients.
s <- structured_penalty(parameters7::log_cholesky(2))
th <- list(log_L1 = 0.1, log_L2 = -0.1, L2.1 = 0.3)
bb <- c(1, -0.5)
penalty_dcross(s, bb, th)$log_L1_log_L1
#> [1] 4.7198354 0.3315513
drop(penalty_d2hessian(s, bb, th)$log_L1_log_L1 %*% bb)
#> [1] 4.7198354 0.3315513
